title: HALSELL COLLEGE AND ITS FOUNDER
text:
HALSELL COLLEGE AND ITS FOUNDER

In eighteen hundred seventy-nine,
Doctors of names and dates
Came to Savoy College right
To build a better fate.

Of modest architecture was
The buildings, made of wood,
With careful, modest campus stood
On spacious campus stood.

In "book" lads, polite proud in good,
O'er buildings full of light,
To make John Savoy long roads
The windows wide and bright.

A goodly, kindly, patient man
Who offered learning's prize,
He gave it to all girls and boys,
In wisdom good and wise.

But to the life, skillless boy,
Who found his mother spread,
When changing parts that morning swept,
Who needs[?] him most instead.

Also, with thy slendersome girls
In petticoat and curl,
Who came[?] to study Maggie Jones,
Felt very nearly indeed.

When chased in her pursuit,
With dancing girls with Maggie Jones,
The who was much the class for you,
You who can advance[?].

To make John Savoy, there she went,
"I was Ann[?], she helped me out,"
Who make that special[?] who found,
A time[?].

Among the girls, there were Kate King,
The Farrars, and the Chenoweths,
And others known to fame.

John Penn, Joe Lacy, Suze Wells,
Jim Crow, Joe Walker, Bob Fent,
Bill Cole, and many more,
When they were caught red-handed at
The blacksmith's store.

The masters then were kind but firm,
With rule, strict but fair,
Who now, are most[?] on the sod,
Or silver[?] in the hair.

—M. MAY.
